title: Runtime Phase Diagram and Fidelity Operational Playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a compact operational contract for how the serving runtime transitions across deterministic phases during normal operation, stress, and failure modes. It codifies: a phase diagram (textual + ASCII timeline) for decision points; fidelity modes and their safe transitions; kernel-scheduler hooks and minimum telemetry signals required for automated decisions; a step-by-step runbook for human intervention; and a lightweight experiment checklist for validating policy changes. This document is intended for runtime engineers, on-call SREs, and product owners responsible for SLOs and quality budgets.

Goals

- Ensure predictable and auditable transitions between runtime fidelity modes (Full, Graceful Degraded, Conservative, Emergency).
- Define the minimal signals and thresholds needed to trigger automated transitions and operator alerts.
- Provide a safe rollback and validation checklist for kernel/scheduler policy changes that affect fidelity.

Scope

- Applies to the primary serving runtime (gpu-dispatcher + kernel-shephard) and the orchestration layer that performs routing/fallback.
- Covers request-level fidelity changes (response length truncation, sampling temperature changes, model variant swap, quantization tiering) and execution-level controls (batch slicing, preemption, slot revocation).
- Excludes client-side retry/backoff policies and upstream model training pipelines.

Phase Diagram (textual)

We model runtime state as a small set of phases that the operator or automation may transition between. Each phase has a clear intent, allowed actions, and required observability.

1) Full (green)
   - Intent: Serve requests at configured model and kernel fidelity with SLO headroom.
   - Allowed actions: Normal batching, full KV cache retention, prefetch enabled, latency SLO = 95th < configured threshold.

2) Graceful Degraded (amber)
   - Intent: Reduce cost/pressure while preserving correctness for high-priority requests.
   - Allowed actions: Apply per-tenant degradation (e.g., lower sampling N, transient model variant with smaller context), reduce prefetch aggressiveness, coalesce small batches, enable fast-path quant kernels.

3) Conservative (orange)
   - Intent: Stop non-essential work, prioritize tail-latency sensitive traffic and safety-critical routes.
   - Allowed actions: Disable background KV prefetch, evict cold KV shards, reduce maximum output tokens, enable stricter admission control quotas.

4) Emergency (red)
   - Intent: Maintain basic availability for critical customers or routes, accept higher unit cost.
   - Allowed actions: Route only to SLA-backed capacity, reduce model size aggressively (e.g., prune/condense context), enable synchronous hedging to reduce tail risk, lift batching to reduce memory pressure.

ASCII timeline (simplified)

  Normal -> (pressure rises: sustained queue depth > Q_high) -> Graceful Degraded -> (kernel errors or memory pressure) -> Conservative -> (data-plane outage or severe capacity loss) -> Emergency
  Emergency -> (capacity restored and health heuristics pass) -> Conservative -> (stability sustained) -> Graceful Degraded -> (fully recovered) -> Normal

Signals and thresholds (minimum set)

- Queue metrics: request_queue_depth (per node), sustained_window = 120s, Q_high = 500, Q_critical = 1500.
- Kernel metrics: kernel_p95_latency (per kernel family), slow_kernel_rate > 2% over 5m -> escalate.
- Memory: gpu_memory_utilization > 92% for 60s -> trigger Conservative.
- Error rates: model_inference_errors > 0.5% 1m OR grpc_stream_resets > 1% 1m -> evaluate for Emergency.
- SLO degradation: observed_p95_latency > target * 1.35 for 3 consecutive evaluation windows (1m windows) -> transition to Graceful Degraded.

Telemetry contract (required fields for automation)

- request.surface: route_id, priority_score, user_tier
- request.metrics: queue_depth, arrival_rate, last_trace_id
- kernel.signals: kernel_family_id, p50/p95/p99, queue_drain_rate
- host.metrics: gpu_mem_pct, cuda_error_count, nvlink_errors
- runtime.health: consul_health, agent_heartbeat, time_since_last_config_apply

Kernel scheduler hooks (implementation notes)

- admission_controller.on_phase_change(phase_name): idempotent call invoked by orchestration layer. Handlers must complete within 2s and return a short summary.
- kernel_mapper.suggest_variant(route_id, phase_name, sample_context): returns kernel_variant_id and expected_resource_delta.
- kvcache.adaptive_eviction(phase_name, eviction_fraction): synchronous call to reduce memory footprint with consistent eviction markers.

Operational runbook: automated transition flow

1) Detection (automation)
   a) Rolling windows: compute windowed aggregates for queue_depth, kernel latency, memory utilization.
   b) If any threshold crossed (see Signals table), automation sends an entry to the decision log and evaluates safe transition rules.
2) Policy evaluation
   a) Run admission policies (priority-aware): ensure top 20% high-priority routes do not drop below configured fidelity threshold.
   b) Compute candidate actions (e.g., enable quantized fast-kernel for model X on pool A).
3) Staging (pre-commit)
   a) Try non-invasive controls first: increase batch coalescing, lower sampling, alpha throttle non-critical routes.
   b) Wait 30s; if improvements observed in p95 latency and queue depth, keep staged changes and record in decision log.
4) Commit
   a) Execute idempotent kernel and routing changes with atomic config tags (config.apply_id).
   b) Emit audit event and notify on-call via Slack pager and runbook link.
5) Monitor
   a) Observe for 5 minutes. If metrics improve, continue; otherwise escalate to human operator for Conservative/Emergency escalation.

Human escalation playbook (short)

- If automation fails to stabilize after a single commit and 2x staging attempts (total 2m), page on-call SRE with subject: "Runtime phase escalate -> node group X". Include decision log id.
- On-call responsibilities:
  1. Verify decision log and applied config changes.
  2. If memory pressure is root cause: run the GPU eviction helper and cross-check NVML diagnostics.
  3. If kernel stalls present: trigger graceful drain of affected node(s) and activate a recovery kernel roll (see Kernel Roll procedure below).

Kernel roll procedure (safe patch for slow kernel family)

1) Quarantine: mark kernel_family.K as quarantine=true in scheduler metadata. Stop assigning new slots.
2) Shadow canary: deploy candidate kernel K' to 2 nodes in shadow pool, mirror a 1% traffic sample (low-priority traffic) for 10 minutes.
3) Compare latencies and error rates against historical baseline using the bench harness (bench-run-id) and the microprobe profile.
4) If K' passes (p95 <= baseline * 1.05 and errors <= baseline), promote K' to 10% traffic, then 30%, then full, with 5m observation windows.
5) If K' fails at any step, roll back immediately and run postmortem tag.

Minimum validation checklist for any scheduler/config change

- Unit tests for mapper and admission_controller change: green.
- End-to-end bench: synthetic replication of traffic shape (spike and tail) using the runtime synthetic runner.
- Canary traffic: 2 nodes, 1% traffic for 10m, metrics inbound to bench-run-id.
- Observability: new signals annotated in telemetry index, alert rule added with known owner.
- Rollback plan: pre-recorded config.apply_id for immediate revert.

Config table (example values)

| Parameter | Recommended default | Notes |
| request_queue_probe_window | 120s | Window used to compute sustained pressure |
| Q_high | 500 | Node-level queue depth for guarded staging |
| Q_critical | 1500 | Escalation to Conservative |
| staging_wait | 30s | Wait time after staging change before commit |
| observe_commit_window | 5m | Monitor after commit before marking resolved |
| high_priority_preserve_pct | 20% | Minimum traffic share preserved at higher fidelity |

(Represented above as a markdown-style table for readability; our telemetry UI expects these params in runtime-config service under /configs/phase_control)

Experiment checklist (for policy changes)

- Define hypothesis and metric delta (p95 latency, error rate, SLO loss) and minimum detectable effect.
- Build synthetic load profile that captures burst shape (spike length, inter-arrival tail).
- Run NOMINAL baseline bench (3 runs) and record bench-run-id.
- Deploy change behind flag; run shadow canary for 15m collecting p50/p95/p99, cuda errs, queue_depth.
- Automatic gating: stop if p99 increases by > 30% or error rate doubles.

Common failure scenarios and suggested mitigations

- Symptom: Sustained high queue depth with low GPU utilization.
  Mitigation: Increase batching and coalesce small requests; verify admission_controller is not misclassifying priorities.

- Symptom: High kernel p95 with bursty small requests.
  Mitigation: Enable fast-path quantized kernels for small-context routes; reduce scheduling jitter by pinning core threads.

- Symptom: Frequent NVML OOMs after deployment.
  Mitigation: Revert recent kernel changes, evict cold KV shards, and enable conservative phase to protect high-priority routing.

Appendix A — Example config footprint (YAML snippet)

---
phase_control:
  window_seconds: 120
  q_high: 500
  q_critical: 1500
  preserve_tiers:
    - tier: enterprise
      preserve_pct: 50
    - tier: standard
      preserve_pct: 20
  staging_wait_seconds: 30
  observe_commit_minutes: 5
---

Appendix B — Quick CLI helpers

- Show decision log: rw-runtimectl decision-log show --limit 50 --since 1h
- Force a phase: rw-runtimectl phase set --node-group gpu-pool-3 --phase graceful-degraded --reason "manual-test"
- Rollback config: rw-runtimectl config revert --apply-id <id>

Notes and change history

- 2025-10-15: Created by Priya Raman to consolidate phase controls and automation contract.
- 2025-12-09: Added kernel roll procedure and quarantine pattern (review by Diego Alvarez).
- 2026-02-18: Added explicit telemetry contract and tightened thresholds for Q_high/Q_critical following a production incident (postmortem ref: PM-2026-03).

This playbook is expected to evolve. If you propose changes, open a PR to the runtime playbook repo and ping the reviewers listed above.
